chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Qasim al-Hadrami, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: Upon every person who gains or earns, the khums of what he acquires is due, for Fatimah عليها السلام and for those from her heirs after her who hold her authority, the proofs over the people. That belongs exclusively to them; they place it wherever they wish. And charity has been forbidden to them.
Even a tailor who sews a shirt for five daniqs—one daniq of it belongs to us, except for whomever among our Shi'ah we have made lawful for them, so that birth may be wholesome for them through it.
Indeed, there is nothing before Allah on the Day of qiyamah greater than zina. Indeed, the صاحب of the khums will stand and say: My Lord, ask these people by what they made lawful marriage relations.

key_terms.الصَّدَقَةُ: charity, which is forbidden to them here
key_terms.الْحُجَجِ: the divine proofs over the people
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: the one-fifth due from gains and earnings
key_terms.الْوِلَادَةُ: birth or lineage being rendered wholesome through lawful means
key_terms.شِيعَتِنَا: our Shi'ah, the followers of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.وَرَثَتِهَا: her heirs, referring here to those who inherit her authority and right
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection and final reckoning

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Istibsar say about the obligation of khums on earnings and its relation to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states the obligation of khums on gains and earnings, and identifies it as a right belonging to Fatimah عليها السلام and the inheriting proofs of Allah over the people from her descendants. It also explains that this right was specially made lawful for certain Shi'ah, and warns of grave accountability on the Day of qiyamah concerning unlawful use of wealth connected to khums.
